title: Finite type near a contracted prime from module-neighbourhood descent
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $K/k$ a field extension [def-pc-field-extension]. For each commutative $k$-algebra $C$ write $C_K=C\otimes_kK$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], and for $v\in C$ write $C_v$ and $M_v$ for ring and module localization at $1,v,v^2,\ldots$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. Assume the following neighbourhood-surjectivity principle [lem-sc-module-surjectivity-field-extension-neighbourhood]: for every commutative $k$-algebra $C$, every $C$-linear map $\varphi:M\to N$ of arbitrary $C$-modules, every $v\in C_K$, and every prime ideal $P\subset C_K$ with $v\notin P$, surjectivity of $(\varphi\otimes_k\mathrm{id}_K)_v$ implies that some $d\in C$ with $d\otimes1\notin P$ makes $\varphi_d:M_d\to N_d$ surjective. Let $A,B$ be commutative $k$-algebras and $\alpha:A\to B$ a $k$-algebra homomorphism. Let $\mathfrak q_K\subset B_K$ be prime, put $\mathfrak q=\{b\in B:b\otimes1\in\mathfrak q_K\}$, and let $u\in B_K\setminus\mathfrak q_K$. If $(B_K)_u$ is a finite type $A_K$-algebra via $\alpha\otimes_k\mathrm{id}_K$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], then there is $c\in B\setminus\mathfrak q$ such that $B_c$ is a finite type $A$-algebra.

proof.text: Choose finite $A_K$-algebra generators $y_1,\ldots,y_r$ of $(B_K)_u$. Write $y_i=z_i/u^{n_i}$ with $z_i\in B_K$. Express $u$ and every $z_i$ as finite sums $\sum_j b_j\otimes\lambda_j$, and collect their finitely many $B$-coefficients into $t_1,\ldots,t_m$. These choices use only the polynomial-generation definition, the fraction construction, and the fact that pure tensors generate the tensor product. Empty lists of generators or coefficients are allowed.

proof.text: Let $C=\alpha(A)[t_1,\ldots,t_m]\subseteq B$, explicitly the subring of polynomial expressions in the $t_j$ with coefficients from $\alpha(A)$. It contains the image of $k$, so is a commutative $k$-algebra. The chosen expressions give elements $v,w_i\in C_K$ mapping to $u,z_i$ under the map $\iota_K:C_K\to B_K$ induced by inclusion. The localized map $F:(C_K)_v\to(B_K)_u$ sends $a/v^n$ to $\iota_K(a)/u^n$. Its image is a subalgebra over $A_K$ (coefficients map through $C_K$), and contains every $y_i=F(w_i/v^{n_i})$. Every polynomial in the $y_i$ therefore belongs to its image, so $F$ is surjective. This uses no injectivity of $\iota_K$.

proof.text:
Put $P=\iota_K^{-1}(\mathfrak q_K)$. This is a prime ideal of $C_K$: its quotient maps injectively to the domain $B_K/\mathfrak q_K$. Since $\iota_K(v)=u
otin\mathfrak q_K$, we have $v
otin P$. Regard $\iota:C	o B$ as a $C$-linear map of $C$-modules. Its scalar extension localized at $v$ is exactly $F$ of Step 2, because on fractions it is $a/v^n\mapsto\iota_K(a)/u^n$; here the action of $v$ on $B_K$ is multiplication by $u$. Apply the neighbourhood-surjectivity principle assumed in the statement, in the precise form of [lem-sc-module-surjectivity-field-extension-neighbourhood], with base algebra $C$, modules $C,B$, map $\iota$, element $v$ and prime $P$. It gives $d\in C$ with $d\otimes1
otin P$ and surjective $\iota_d:C_d	o B_{\iota(d)}$. Set $c=\iota(d)\in B$. Then $c\otimes1=\iota_K(d\otimes1)
otin\mathfrak q_K$, so $c
otin\mathfrak q$. No finiteness of $B$ as a $C$-module is needed.

proof.text: For any $x\in B_c$, surjectivity gives $x=\iota_d(g/d^n)=g(t_1,\ldots,t_m)/c^n$ for some $g\in C$, written as a polynomial with coefficients in $\alpha(A)$. Thus $x=g(t_1/1,\ldots,t_m/1)(1/c)^n$. Consequently $t_1/1,\ldots,t_m/1,1/c$ generate $B_c$ as an $A$-algebra. By the finite-type definition, $B_c$ is of finite type over $A$, and Step 3 gives the required $c\notin\mathfrak q$.

Source: Stacks 00QP (algebra.tex:31443) uses a coefficient subalgebra; this delivery replaces 00QP's global faithful-flatness step with the assumed principle applied to the inclusion C into B, and is marked by=agent. The assumed principle is true: Spec C_K -> Spec C is open (0383), local maps are faithfully flat, so D(v) maps to an open set disjoint from Supp coker, and a D(d) inside it gives coker_d = 0. So the hypothesis is not vacuous. Step 1: generators z_i/u^{n_i}, pure-tensor coefficients t_j. Step 2: C = alpha(A)[t] is a k-algebra; v and w_i lift; F is well defined because iota_K(v) = u; A_K factors through C_K, so F is surjective, without using injectivity. Step 3: P = iota_K^{-1}(q_K) is prime and v is not in P; localizing the C_K-module B_K at v gives (B_K)_u, so the principle applies to the C-linear map C -> B for arbitrary modules. It gives d with c = iota(d) and c⊗1 not in q_K. Step 4: t_j/1 and 1/c generate B_c over A, through the original alpha. Edge cases checked: K = k, u = 1, empty lists, B = 0 (vacuous), zero divisors. The parent lem-sc-lfp-field-extension-pointwise-descent Step 2 uses exactly this statement. Duplicate check: lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-descends-faithfully-flat and the fpqc-descend-locally-finite-type node are global descent, not this pointwise statement.
